I stopped the bootstrap-greenfield pipeline at Phase 1 (Confirm Greenfield). The repository already has code, so the pipeline can't run here. I wrote, changed and committed nothing.

**Why it stopped**

I ran the greenfield check (`fragment-check-greenfield-repository`), which only reads files. It found two files that make this repository not greenfield:

| File | Reason |
| --- | --- |
| `package.json` | It declares a build: package `tally`, with a `start` script that runs `node src/server.js`. |
| `src/server.js` | It is application code outside the allowed files: a Node `node:http` server on port 3000 that counts visits. |

The pipeline's rule is to stop before any write when the repository is not greenfield. Because the result was negative, I didn't continue to sort the setup files into missing, placeholder or established.

**Use this instead: `pipeline-bootstrap-workspace`** (the `pipes.bootstrap-workspace` skill). It works from what the code actually shows, and `pipeline-define-codebase-stack` would replace the placeholder `project.md` with the real stack: Node.js with a plain `node:http` server and no frameworks.

If you really want a greenfield setup, the only way is to delete `package.json` and `src/server.js` first and then run bootstrap-greenfield again. The check offers no override, and with existing code the workspace bootstrap is the better fit.
